Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $38 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members. Attorneys’ fees and expenses would be paid separately, subject to court approval; any amount not awarded would go to the class. This offers meaningful, prompt relief without a claims process.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments are appropriate given Brightline’s records. Your proposed $42 million total exceeds our settlement authority. In light of unresolved certification and merits risks, we offer the following terms, with fees subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet, subject to court approval. Automatic payments to all identified class members and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class are important protections.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We propose a $35 million class fund distributed automatically to all identified members. Fees and expenses would be separately subject to court approval, with any amount not awarded added to the class fund. We are prepared to discuss the fund amount in light of litigation and certification risks, but a claims process is unnecessary given Brightline's records.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We agree a claims process is unnecessary. Although your proposal reaches $40 million, we need to account for litigation risk and negotiate the total outlay. We offer automatic distribution and court-reviewed fees on the following terms.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We accept your latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund with automatic distribution, $4 million in separately court-reviewed fees, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We will work with you to submit it for court approval.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached this settlement through arm’s-length negotiations. The agreement provides a $30 million class fund, with payments made automatically to identified class members, and a separate $4 million request for attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. The fund offers prompt, substantial relief despite the risks of class certification and trial.
